text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card (27.2%, 3.1%, 18.31, 4.31, 33%, 0 records). The cautious, inconclusive stance fits the zero documentation returned, and the next steps are concrete (a random sample of 30 charts plus targeted 99215s). The headline is clear but gives no signal strength. The summary is thin on specifics, though. It leaves out the 8.65x ratio and the roughly 300 excess 99215 claims. It also omits the complexity gradient (13.5% at 0 conditions rising to 61% at 5+), which is the most informative evidence on billed level versus patient complexity. The wording 'too few returned records' is slightly off, since none were returned. The 'no usable charts' next step is sound, but only 2 example claims are cited, both 0-condition patients. The summary also does not note that the high-complexity 99215s are plausible, so it gives no balance. The 'if no response' step is reasonable but vague about what follows.
